PE SP26 Paper 1 (music database) — Q2–Q7 and Q10, graded in the browser

DBI202 · real Practical Exam SP26 Paper 1 · the paper's own DBscript.sql (30 artists, 300+ tracks) · 1 mark per question

1. Overview

The real SP26 Paper 1 on the music database (Artists → Albums → Tracks ← Genres; Users → Playlists → PlaylistTracks). The plain-SQL questions are graded here on the paper's exact data and again on a modified copy. Q1 (ERD with nvarchar, composite and multi-valued attributes, a subclass), Q8 (procedure) and Q9 (trigger) are the second exercise of this lesson, on your own SQL Server.

General requirements

  • One file per question containing ONLY the statement that answers it — no USE, no GO, no test commands (one violation = 0 for the question in the real exam).
  • Portable SQL only here: write a year filter as a date range (no YEAR()), no TOP, no ISNULL. The file names keep the paper's numbers.
  • Row order is graded only where both engines agree. Where NULLs take part in the ORDER BY (Q4) the order is not graded: SQL Server sorts NULL first, PostgreSQL last.

4. Functional requirements

1. Q2 · Tracks whose title contains "love" 1 mark

All tracks whose title contains the string "love", not case-sensitive.

Requirements:

  • Columns: ID, Title, Duration, Language, AlbumID, GenreID. Any row order. LOWER(Title) makes it case-insensitive on every collation.

2. Q3 · 2020 tracks by female artists from the USA 1 mark

Tracks of albums released in 2020 and performed by female artists from the USA.

Requirements:

  • Columns: ID, TrackTitle, AlbumTitle, ReleaseYear, ArtistName, Gender, Country. Any row order.

3. Q4 · Rock tracks after 2020 and their playlists (even none) 1 mark

Tracks of albums released after 2020 in the genre 'Rock', with the playlists they were added to. A track in no playlist still appears (playlist columns NULL).

Requirements:

  • Columns: AlbumTitle, ReleaseYear, TrackID, TrackTitle, GenreName, PlaylistTitle, AddedDate. The paper sorts by PlaylistTitle DESC, TrackTitle; the order is not graded here (NULL ordering differs between engines).

4. Q5 · Every artist: albums 2020–2024 and their Rock tracks 1 mark

Every artist with the number of albums released between 2020 and 2024 (inclusive) and the number of 'Rock' tracks in those albums — 0 when none.

Requirements:

  • Columns: ArtistID, Name, Gender, Country, NumberOfAlbums, NumberOfTracks, ordered by ArtistID.

5. Q6 · Canadian artists: album(s) with the most tracks 1 mark

For each artist whose Country is 'Canada', the album(s) with the highest number of tracks among that artist's albums. Ties are all shown; an artist without albums is not shown.

Requirements:

  • Columns: ArtistID, ArtistName, AlbumID, AlbumTitle, NumberOfTracks, ordered by ArtistID, AlbumID.

6. Q7 · Per country: the album leading in all-time AND 2023 playlist additions 1 mark

For each country, the album(s) of that country's artists that have BOTH the highest total number of playlist additions (all years) AND the highest number of additions in 2023, among the albums of the same country.

Requirements:

  • Columns: Country, AlbumID, AlbumTitle, TotalPlaylistAdditions, TotalPlaylistAdditionsIn2023, ordered by Country, AlbumTitle. The year as a date range: AddedDate >= '2023-01-01' AND AddedDate < '2024-01-01'.

7. Q10 · Add every 'Stars Dance' track to playlist 10 1 mark

Insert rows into PlaylistTracks so that all tracks of the album titled 'Stars Dance' are added to the playlist with ID = 10, with AddedDate = 6 March 2026 (date only).

Requirements:

  • One INSERT … SELECT; find the album by its title.

1. Tổng quan

Đề SP26 Paper 1 thật trên CSDL nhạc (Artists → Albums → Tracks ← Genres; Users → Playlists → PlaylistTracks). Các câu SQL thuần được chấm ở đây trên đúng dữ liệu của đề và trên một bản đã sửa. Q1 (ERD với nvarchar, thuộc tính phức hợp, đa trị, lớp con), Q8 (procedure) và Q9 (trigger) là bài thứ hai của bài học này, chạy trên SQL Server của bạn.

Yêu cầu chung

  • Mỗi câu một tệp CHỈ chứa câu lệnh trả lời — không USE, không GO, không lệnh chạy thử (thi thật: sai một điều là 0 điểm câu đó).
  • Ở đây chỉ dùng SQL chạy cả hai hệ: lọc năm bằng khoảng ngày (không YEAR()), không TOP, không ISNULL. Tên tệp giữ đúng số câu của đề.
  • Thứ tự dòng chỉ chấm ở câu mà hai hệ cho cùng kết quả. Câu có NULL trong ORDER BY (Q4) không chấm thứ tự: SQL Server xếp NULL đầu, PostgreSQL xếp cuối.

4. Yêu cầu chức năng

1. Q2 · Bài hát có tên chứa "love" 1 điểm

Mọi bài hát có tên chứa chuỗi "love", không phân biệt hoa thường.

Yêu cầu:

  • Cột: ID, Title, Duration, Language, AlbumID, GenreID. Thứ tự dòng tuỳ ý. LOWER(Title) giúp không phân biệt hoa thường với mọi collation.

2. Q3 · Bài hát năm 2020 của nữ nghệ sĩ Mỹ 1 điểm

Bài hát thuộc album phát hành năm 2020 của nữ nghệ sĩ đến từ Mỹ.

Yêu cầu:

  • Cột: ID, TrackTitle, AlbumTitle, ReleaseYear, ArtistName, Gender, Country. Thứ tự dòng tuỳ ý.

3. Q4 · Bài Rock sau 2020 và playlist chứa chúng (kể cả không có) 1 điểm

Bài hát thuộc album phát hành sau 2020, thể loại 'Rock', kèm các playlist đã thêm chúng. Bài không nằm trong playlist nào vẫn hiện (cột playlist NULL).

Yêu cầu:

  • Cột: AlbumTitle, ReleaseYear, TrackID, TrackTitle, GenreName, PlaylistTitle, AddedDate. Đề sắp theo PlaylistTitle giảm, TrackTitle; ở đây không chấm thứ tự (hai hệ xếp NULL khác nhau).

4. Q5 · Mọi nghệ sĩ: album 2020–2024 và số bài Rock trong đó 1 điểm

Mọi nghệ sĩ kèm số album phát hành từ 2020 tới 2024 (gồm hai đầu) và số bài 'Rock' trong các album đó — 0 nếu không có.

Yêu cầu:

  • Cột: ArtistID, Name, Gender, Country, NumberOfAlbums, NumberOfTracks, sắp theo ArtistID.

5. Q6 · Nghệ sĩ Canada: (các) album nhiều bài nhất 1 điểm

Với mỗi nghệ sĩ có Country = 'Canada', (các) album có nhiều bài nhất trong các album của nghệ sĩ đó. Hoà thì hiện hết; nghệ sĩ không có album thì không hiện.

Yêu cầu:

  • Cột: ArtistID, ArtistName, AlbumID, AlbumTitle, NumberOfTracks, sắp theo ArtistID, AlbumID.

6. Q7 · Mỗi nước: album dẫn đầu cả tổng lượt thêm vào playlist LẪN lượt năm 2023 1 điểm

Với mỗi nước, (các) album của nghệ sĩ nước đó vừa có tổng lượt được thêm vào playlist (mọi năm) cao nhất VỪA có lượt thêm năm 2023 cao nhất, trong các album cùng nước.

Yêu cầu:

  • Cột: Country, AlbumID, AlbumTitle, TotalPlaylistAdditions, TotalPlaylistAdditionsIn2023, sắp theo Country, AlbumTitle. Năm viết bằng khoảng ngày: AddedDate >= '2023-01-01' AND AddedDate < '2024-01-01'.

7. Q10 · Thêm mọi bài của 'Stars Dance' vào playlist 10 1 điểm

Chèn dòng vào PlaylistTracks để mọi bài của album tên 'Stars Dance' được thêm vào playlist ID = 10, AddedDate = 6/3/2026 (chỉ ngày).

Yêu cầu:

  • Một INSERT … SELECT; tìm album theo tên.

-- DBscript.sql: sample schema + data of this task (READ ONLY — the grader loads it by itself; editing this tab changes nothing).
-- DBscript.sql: lược đồ + dữ liệu mẫu của bài (CHỈ ĐỂ ĐỌC — máy chấm tự nạp; sửa tab này không ảnh hưởng gì).
-- Written in SQL Server syntax, like the PE's DBscript.sql — runs as-is in SSMS.
CREATE TABLE Artists (
    ID INT PRIMARY KEY,
    Name NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
	Gender nvarchar(20),
    Country NVARCHAR(50),
    Birthdate date
);

-- 2. Albums Table
CREATE TABLE Albums (
    ID INT PRIMARY KEY,
    Title NVARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    ReleaseYear INT CHECK (ReleaseYear > 1900),
    ArtistID INT REFERENCES Artists(ID)
);

-- 3. Genres Table
CREATE TABLE Genres (
    ID INT PRIMARY KEY,
    Name NVARCHAR(50) UNIQUE NOT NULL
);

-- 4. Tracks Table
CREATE TABLE Tracks (
    ID INT PRIMARY KEY,
    Title NVARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    Duration INT NOT NULL, -- Duration in seconds
	Language nvarchar(100),
    AlbumID INT REFERENCES Albums(ID),
    GenreID INT REFERENCES Genres(ID)
);

-- 5. Users Table
CREATE TABLE Users (
    ID INT PRIMARY KEY,
    Username NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    Email VARCHAR(100) UNIQUE,
    SubscriptionType NVARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'Free' CHECK (SubscriptionType IN ('Free', 'Premium')),
    RegistrationDate DATE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

-- 6. Playlists Table
CREATE TABLE Playlists (
    ID INT PRIMARY KEY,
    Title NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    UserID INT REFERENCES Users(ID),
    CreatedAt DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

-- 7. PlaylistTracks
CREATE TABLE PlaylistTracks (
    PlaylistID INT REFERENCES Playlists(ID),
    TrackID INT REFERENCES Tracks(ID),
    AddedDate DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    PRIMARY KEY (PlaylistID, TrackID)
);

SELECT t.ID, t.Title AS TrackTitle, al.Title AS AlbumTitle, al.ReleaseYear,
       ar.Name AS ArtistName, ar.Gender, ar.Country
FROM Tracks t
JOIN Albums  al ON al.ID = t.AlbumID
JOIN Artists ar ON ar.ID = al.ArtistID
WHERE al.ReleaseYear = 2020
  AND ar.Gender = 'Female'
  AND ar.Country = 'USA';

solutionCodeJson.name: Q3.sql
solutionCodeJson.code:
SELECT al.Title AS AlbumTitle, al.ReleaseYear, t.ID AS TrackID, t.Title AS TrackTitle,
       g.Name AS GenreName, p.Title AS PlaylistTitle, pt.AddedDate
FROM Tracks t
JOIN Albums al ON al.ID = t.AlbumID
JOIN Genres g  ON g.ID  = t.GenreID
LEFT JOIN PlaylistTracks pt ON pt.TrackID = t.ID          -- keep tracks without playlists
LEFT JOIN Playlists p       ON p.ID = pt.PlaylistID
WHERE al.ReleaseYear > 2020
  AND g.Name = 'Rock'
ORDER BY PlaylistTitle DESC, TrackTitle ASC;

solutionCodeJson.name: Q4.sql
solutionCodeJson.code:
SELECT ar.ID AS ArtistID, ar.Name, ar.Gender, ar.Country,
       COUNT(DISTINCT al.ID) AS NumberOfAlbums,
       COUNT(t.ID)          AS NumberOfTracks
FROM Artists ar
LEFT JOIN Albums al ON al.ArtistID = ar.ID AND al.ReleaseYear BETWEEN 2020 AND 2024   -- filters of the optional side go in ON
LEFT JOIN Tracks t  ON t.AlbumID = al.ID
                   AND t.GenreID IN (SELECT ID FROM Genres WHERE Name = 'Rock')
GROUP BY ar.ID, ar.Name, ar.Gender, ar.Country
ORDER BY ar.ID;

solutionCodeJson.name: Q5.sql
solutionCodeJson.code:
WITH AlbumCount AS (
    SELECT ar.ID AS ArtistID, ar.Name AS ArtistName, al.ID AS AlbumID, al.Title AS AlbumTitle,
           COUNT(t.ID) AS NumberOfTracks
    FROM Artists ar
    JOIN Albums al     ON al.ArtistID = ar.ID
    LEFT JOIN Tracks t ON t.AlbumID = al.ID
    WHERE ar.Country = 'Canada'
    GROUP BY ar.ID, ar.Name, al.ID, al.Title
)
SELECT ArtistID, ArtistName, AlbumID, AlbumTitle, NumberOfTracks
FROM AlbumCount a
WHERE NumberOfTracks = (SELECT MAX(NumberOfTracks) FROM AlbumCount b WHERE b.ArtistID = a.ArtistID)   -- max of THIS artist
ORDER BY ArtistID, AlbumID;

solutionCodeJson.name: Q6.sql
solutionCodeJson.code:
WITH AlbumStats AS (
    SELECT ar.Country, al.ID AS AlbumID, al.Title AS AlbumTitle,
           COUNT(pt.TrackID) AS TotalPlaylistAdditions,
           SUM(CASE WHEN pt.AddedDate >= '2023-01-01' AND pt.AddedDate < '2024-01-01' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS TotalPlaylistAdditionsIn2023
    FROM Artists ar
    JOIN Albums al ON al.ArtistID = ar.ID
    JOIN Tracks t  ON t.AlbumID = al.ID
    LEFT JOIN PlaylistTracks pt ON pt.TrackID = t.ID
    GROUP BY ar.Country, al.ID, al.Title
)
SELECT Country, AlbumID, AlbumTitle, TotalPlaylistAdditions, TotalPlaylistAdditionsIn2023
FROM AlbumStats a
WHERE TotalPlaylistAdditions       = (SELECT MAX(TotalPlaylistAdditions)       FROM AlbumStats b WHERE b.Country = a.Country)
  AND TotalPlaylistAdditionsIn2023 = (SELECT MAX(TotalPlaylistAdditionsIn2023) FROM AlbumStats b WHERE b.Country = a.Country)
ORDER BY Country ASC, AlbumTitle ASC;

    Name NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
	Gender nvarchar(20),
    Country NVARCHAR(50),
    Birthdate date
);

-- 2. Albums Table
CREATE TABLE Albums (
    ID INT PRIMARY KEY,
    Title NVARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    ReleaseYear INT CHECK (ReleaseYear > 1900),
    ArtistID INT REFERENCES Artists(ID)
);

-- 3. Genres Table
CREATE TABLE Genres (
    ID INT PRIMARY KEY,
    Name NVARCHAR(50) UNIQUE NOT NULL
);

-- 4. Tracks Table
CREATE TABLE Tracks (
    ID INT PRIMARY KEY,
    Title NVARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    Duration INT NOT NULL, -- Duration in seconds
	Language nvarchar(100),
    AlbumID INT REFERENCES Albums(ID),
    GenreID INT REFERENCES Genres(ID)
);

-- 5. Users Table
CREATE TABLE Users (
    ID INT PRIMARY KEY,
    Username NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    Email VARCHAR(100) UNIQUE,
    SubscriptionType NVARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'Free' CHECK (SubscriptionType IN ('Free', 'Premium')),
    RegistrationDate DATE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

-- 6. Playlists Table
CREATE TABLE Playlists (
    ID INT PRIMARY KEY,
    Title NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    UserID INT REFERENCES Users(ID),
    CreatedAt DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

-- 7. PlaylistTracks
CREATE TABLE PlaylistTracks (
    PlaylistID INT REFERENCES Playlists(ID),
    TrackID INT REFERENCES Tracks(ID),
    AddedDate DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    PRIMARY KEY (PlaylistID, TrackID)
);

CREATE TABLE Artists (
    ID INT PRIMARY KEY,
    Name NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
	Gender nvarchar(20),
    Country NVARCHAR(50),
    Birthdate date
);

-- 2. Albums Table
CREATE TABLE Albums (
    ID INT PRIMARY KEY,
    Title NVARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    ReleaseYear INT CHECK (ReleaseYear > 1900),
    ArtistID INT REFERENCES Artists(ID)
);

-- 3. Genres Table
CREATE TABLE Genres (
    ID INT PRIMARY KEY,
    Name NVARCHAR(50) UNIQUE NOT NULL
);

-- 4. Tracks Table
CREATE TABLE Tracks (
    ID INT PRIMARY KEY,
    Title NVARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    Duration INT NOT NULL, -- Duration in seconds
	Language nvarchar(100),
    AlbumID INT REFERENCES Albums(ID),
    GenreID INT REFERENCES Genres(ID)
);

-- 5. Users Table
CREATE TABLE Users (
    ID INT PRIMARY KEY,
    Username NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    Email VARCHAR(100) UNIQUE,
    SubscriptionType NVARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'Free' CHECK (SubscriptionType IN ('Free', 'Premium')),
    RegistrationDate DATE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

-- 6. Playlists Table
CREATE TABLE Playlists (
    ID INT PRIMARY KEY,
    Title NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    UserID INT REFERENCES Users(ID),
    CreatedAt DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

-- 7. PlaylistTracks
CREATE TABLE PlaylistTracks (
    PlaylistID INT REFERENCES Playlists(ID),
    TrackID INT REFERENCES Tracks(ID),
    AddedDate DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    PRIMARY KEY (PlaylistID, TrackID)
);

exercises.problemHtml:
The T-SQL half of the real SP26 Paper 1. setup.sql loads the paper's DBscript.sql (music database, IDENTITY keys).

  1. Q1 — ERD: Universities(universityID int, name nvarchar(200), address = {street nvarchar(50), city nvarchar(50)}) 1 —workFor— N Employees(empID int, FullName nvarchar(60), gender nvarchar(10), phone nvarchar(20) multi-valued); Professors isA Employees with field nvarchar(100), N —workFor— 1 Departments(depID int, name nvarchar(100)). Multi-valued attribute table = table name + attribute name; subclass in ER style.
  2. Q8 — listTopArtistByYear @year int: for each country, the artist(s) with the most playlist additions in that year (ties all shown): Country, ArtistID, ArtistName, TotalPlaylistAdditionsInYear.
  3. Q9 — tr_insertPlaylist on Playlists: unknown UserID ⇒ not inserted; CreatedAt between the user's RegistrationDate and now ⇒ kept; otherwise ⇒ replaced by the current datetime. Several rows at once.

Runs on YOUR SQL Server, not in the browser. Q1 needs nvarchar exactly as the ERD says, Q8 is a stored procedure and Q9 an INSTEAD OF trigger using GETDATE() — SQL Server–only, checked on your own server with the paper's DBscript.sql. Nothing here is graded automatically: run the self-check check.sql on your machine and, when it prints ALL 8 CHECKS PASSED, press Mark as solved.

How to run it (Windows or macOS)

Press Tải .zip (download) above the code and unzip it. The folder has three files: setup.sql (re-creates a scratch database DBI202_CL with the sample tables), solution.sql (YOUR answer — edit only this one) and check.sql (8 checks; prints PASS/FAIL for each and ends with ALL 8 CHECKS PASSED). Always run them in this order: setup → solution → check.

  • Windows + SSMS (the course setup, lesson 0.3): open setup.sql → F5; open solution.sql → F5; open check.sql → F5, then read the Messages tab. Or in a terminal inside the folder (sqlcmd ships with SQL Server; otherwise winget install sqlcmd):
    sqlcmd -S localhost -E -C -i setup.sql,solution.sql,check.sql (use -U sa -P "<password>" instead of -E for a SQL login).
  • macOS (SQL Server in Docker, as in lesson 0.3 — Apple Silicon: mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sql-edge, Intel: mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2022-latest):
    docker run -d --name dbi202-sql -e ACCEPT_EULA=Y -e "MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD=Dbi202#Lab" -p 1433:1433 mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sql-edge
    then install the command-line client once with brew install sqlcmd and, inside the folder:
    sqlcmd -S localhost,1433 -U sa -P "Dbi202#Lab" -C -i setup.sql,solution.sql,check.sql
    (or open the three files in VS Code with the SQL Server (mssql) extension and run them in the same order).

Use CREATE OR ALTER for procedures, functions, triggers and views so that you can run solution.sql again and again. In the real PE you submit only the CREATE … statement, without GO or test commands.

Requirements

  • In the exam each answer is its own file without GO; here solution.sql separates them with GO.
  • Q8 and Q9 are checked against the paper's data and its 4-row INSERT test.

-- Q1
CREATE TABLE Universities (
    universityID int PRIMARY KEY,
    name         nvarchar(200),
    street       nvarchar(50),            -- composite attribute address ⇒ its parts become columns
    city         nvarchar(50)
);
CREATE TABLE Departments (
    depID int PRIMARY KEY,
    name  nvarchar(100)
);
CREATE TABLE Employees (
    empID        int PRIMARY KEY,
    FullName     nvarchar(60),
    gender       nvarchar(10),
    universityID int REFERENCES Universities(universityID)       -- workFor 1–N
);
CREATE TABLE EmployeesPhone (                                      -- multi-valued phone ⇒ table name + attribute
    empID int REFERENCES Employees(empID),
    phone nvarchar(20),
    PRIMARY KEY (empID, phone)
);
CREATE TABLE Professors (                                          -- isA (ER style): PK is also FK to the superclass
    empID int PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES Employees(empID),
    field nvarchar(100),
    depID int REFERENCES Departments(depID)                         -- workFor N–1 Departments
);
GO
-- Q8
CREATE PROCEDURE listTopArtistByYear
    @year int
AS
BEGIN
    WITH ArtistTotals AS (
        SELECT ar.Country, ar.ID AS ArtistID, ar.Name AS ArtistName,
               COUNT(pt.TrackID) AS TotalPlaylistAdditionsInYear
        FROM Artists ar
        LEFT JOIN Albums al         ON al.ArtistID = ar.ID
        LEFT JOIN Tracks t          ON t.AlbumID = al.ID
        LEFT JOIN PlaylistTracks pt ON pt.TrackID = t.ID AND YEAR(pt.AddedDate) = @year
        GROUP BY ar.Country, ar.ID, ar.Name
    )
    SELECT Country, ArtistID, ArtistName, TotalPlaylistAdditionsInYear
    FROM ArtistTotals a
    WHERE TotalPlaylistAdditionsInYear =
          (SELECT MAX(TotalPlaylistAdditionsInYear) FROM ArtistTotals b WHERE b.Country = a.Country)
    ORDER BY ArtistID;
END
GO
-- Q9
CREATE TRIGGER tr_insertPlaylist ON Playlists
INSTEAD OF INSERT
AS
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO Playlists (Title, UserID, CreatedAt)
    SELECT i.Title,
           i.UserID,
           CASE WHEN i.CreatedAt >= u.RegistrationDate AND i.CreatedAt <= GETDATE()
                THEN i.CreatedAt
                ELSE GETDATE()
           END
    FROM inserted i
    JOIN Users u ON u.ID = i.UserID;            -- an unknown UserID is dropped: not inserted
END

    AlbumID INT FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES Albums(ID),

);

    Username NVARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    Email VARCHAR(100) UNIQUE,
    SubscriptionType NVARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'Free' CHECK (SubscriptionType IN ('Free', 'Premium')),

);

    ID INT PRIMARY KEY IDENTITY(1,1),
    Title NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    UserID INT FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES Users(ID),
    CreatedAt DATETIME DEFAULT GETDATE()
);

    PlaylistID INT FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES Playlists(ID),
